author: Marco Bernardini
attribution: Photo: Marco Bernardini, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons. Source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Ecrivain_public_sign_in_Tunisia.jpg. License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/. Unmodified original.
notes: Hand-painted red sign over a public letter-writer's door, Douz (photographed in 2002; the file is a scan of the photographer's own colour print, not a document). Calligraphic Arabic: the first word joins 'بن يحي' into one word 'بنيحي'. The Latin is hand-lettered with a rounded 'E' and the word 'PUBLIC' is set lower than 'ECRIVAIN'; inkwell-and-quill drawings in the corners. location is where the photo was taken (Commons camera coordinates), not the target.

author: Sami Mlouhi
attribution: Photo: Sami Mlouhi, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons. Source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Hammem_El_Siouda_photo_4_%D8%AD%D9%85%D8%A7%D9%85_%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B5%D9%8A%D9%88%D8%AF%D8%A9.jpg. License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/. Unmodified original.
notes: Painted lettering on the facade of a public bathhouse, Place Sidi El Bahri, Tunis; 1280 px image. Arabic is split across the arches (حمّام right, الصّيودة left) with small shadda marks over م and ص. A pedestrian partly overlaps the 'BA' of BAIN; parked vans in front, one with Tunisie Telecom 'TT' branding (distractor). location is where the photo was taken (Commons camera coordinates), not the target.
source_title: File:Hammem El Siouda photo 4 حمام الصيودة.jpg

author: Rusty Clark ~ 100K Photos
attribution: Photo: Rusty Clark ~ 100K Photos, CC BY 2.0, via Flickr. Source: https://www.flickr.com/photos/23206546@N04/6839350074. License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/2.0/. Unmodified original.
notes: Pharmacy in Sousse: green rooftop letters (script 'Pharmacie' + Arabic) and two green awnings with the name in French and Arabic. Distractors at right: 'عالم النظارات / Mondial Optic' rooftop sign, 'OPTICIEN / Adaptation de lentilles de contact' and 'نظارات طبية' awnings with a phone number. Parked cars in the foreground are incidental. Source is 1024 px.

author: eugenijusr
attribution: Photo: eugenijusr, CC BY 2.0, via Flickr. Source: https://www.flickr.com/photos/24172628@N08/2512136716. License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/2.0/. Unmodified original.
notes: Stack of four white arrow panels at night (Port El Kantaoui), lit by flash/street light; Tunis and Hergla to the right, Sousse and Hammam Sousse to the left. Any panel name is a valid place query. Car light trails in the background.

author: Rusty Clark
attribution: Photo: Rusty Clark, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons. Source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Sign_at_the_amphitheatre_of_El_Jem.jpg. License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/2.0/. Unmodified original.
notes: Free-standing wayfinding totem inside the amphitheatre of El Jem, angled to the camera. Header (with UNESCO World Heritage emblem) names the site in small type; the large text is the direction to the tiers, with a left arrow. A scratch runs through 'مدارج' and 'GRADINS', letters intact. The amphitheatre plan and tiny 'Vous êtes ici / You are here' labels at the bottom are not transcribed.
source_title: File:Sign at the amphitheatre of El Jem.jpg
source_categories: Vomitorium of the amphitheatre of El Jem

author: Emna Mizouni
attribution: Photo: Emna Mizouni, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons. Source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Beb_Brikcha_sign_2.jpg. License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/. Unmodified original.
notes: National Heritage Institute glass plaque on the medina wall of Monastir (Commons title: Beb Brikcha sign). The printed film is peeling, so the ministry and institute names (top left 'المعهد الوطني للتراث / Institut National du Patrimoine', top right ministry line) are partly lost and not transcribed; the 'Patrimoine National / تراث وطني' logo text is also skipped. The bottom Arabic line ('معلم مرتب: أمر 218 بتاريخ', classified monument: decree 218 dated) is not transcribed separately. Sun and shadow fall across the plaque.

author: Rawen Ab
attribution: Photo: Rawen Ab, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons. Source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:I_LOVE_TOZEUR_SIGN.jpg. License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/. Unmodified original.
notes: Free-standing white 3-D letters with a red heart in front of a whitewashed shop window in Tozeur; the heart is a shape, written here as ♥. Strong lens flare streak across the left part. Distractor: 'Boulangerie Pâtisserie Ben Bder' fascia at left (partly cut off). Borderline: a city-love sign rather than a name board, but it names the town.
source_categories: I love (heart) city signs in Tozeur

author: Sami Mlouhi
attribution: Photo: Sami Mlouhi, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons. Source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Rue_Ben_Nedjma_%D9%86%D9%87%D8%AC_%D8%A8%D9%86_%D9%86%D8%AC%D9%85%D8%A9.jpg. License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/. Unmodified original.
notes: Blue enamel medina street plate (Tunis), seen from slightly below. The Arabic is in a cursive Maghrebi hand: the last word ends in a long stroke with an upturned hook and no visible dots, so it is transcribed نجمه, although the Commons title spells it نجمة; a small mark above its first letter may be a damma. Checker please confirm the last letter. A chip in the enamel crosses the U of RUE. location is where the photo was taken (Commons camera coordinates), not the target.
source_title: File:Rue Ben Nedjma نهج بن نجمة.jpg
source_categories: Street signs in the medina of Tunis
